source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including all written/read and other notes, not normalized reconstructions.
source.public_versification_note: Public Joshua 9–17 and Hebrew source references align one to one. All 256 original source records are bound exactly once.

authoring_review.review_type: Translation authoring and focused self-check; no independent reviewer or reader testing.

completed_work: Source-first connected draft of nine complete chapters: 256 verses, each with before/after wording, TSW comparator, exact original Hebrew record hash and individual rationale.
Selective Notes and Vocabulary maintain recurring biblical terms and explain consequential uncertainty.
The campaign repetitions, sun-and-moon poem, all royal entries and geographical lists remain present.
All 47 cumulative ledger audits passed, totaling 6,402 verses across 209 chapters. Structural, translation-family, focused assertions, name-order checks and diff checks passed.
key_decisions: 9:4 retains a traditional envoy interpretation of the difficult pinned verb with the provisions-reading alternative noted. 9:14 does not specify tasting or inspecting.
9 keeps the Gibeonites’ fear of death, binding oath, curse and enduring enslavement; service language is distinguished by context.
10:10 keeps the LORD as continuing grammatical subject, notes the possible agent shift; 10:12–13 retains the poem and cosmic imagery without a physical explanation.
10:15,43 retain identical return notices in their given positions. 10:26 explicitly places killing before hanging on five trees; sunset removal follows.
10–11 keep exhaustive destruction statements, all breathing victims, named survivors and remaining peoples. Horse hamstringing is not euphemized.
11:20 preserves divine hardening and no mercy; 11:23’s whole-land rest remains beside 13:1’s unfinished possession.
12 keeps every one in the thirty-one-king tally, Shimron-meron as one entry, Lasharon and Goiim in Gilgal with notes.
13 distinguishes Levi’s offerings inheritance from the LORD himself, retains the half-tribes and sixty Jair settlements, and documents Lidbir and boundary syntax.
14 retains Caleb’s forty, forty-five and eighty-five figures and the perhaps in his request.
15 retains Othniel’s ambiguous kinship phrase, Achsah’s agency and both springs; the implied Othniel in 15:18 is made explicit while noting the alternate referent.

15 retains the name lists despite stated totals of twenty-nine and fourteen that differ from the listed thirty-six and fifteen. Source spellings Lahmas, Kiriath-sannah and reading-tradition Janum are preserved.
16 retains Bethel-to-Luz and difficult boundary syntax with notes; Ephraim’s enclaves and Canaanite forced labor remain.
17 retains all five daughters and their lineage, ten portions, town-versus-land ownership, six named places with the uncertain three heights, and the iron-chariot obstacle.
remaining_review_questions: The three heights at 17:11 and discrepancies in Joshua 15’s town totals remain unresolved.
Joshua’s recurring vocabulary, boundary descriptions and conquest/remaining-land statements need whole-book authoring consistency review after chapters 18–24.
Reader comprehension and sustained listening have not been tested; similarity metrics cannot certify independent authorship, fidelity or biblical fluency.
overlap_qualification: Normalized whole-verse overlap is triage only, not fidelity, originality, comprehension or independent approval.
